Freeze specimen-local preprocessing for counts or Ct measurements

Source: R/singlesample-frozen-preprocessing.R
fit_singlesample_preprocessor.Rd

Records an ordered feature universe and conversion constants. No training means, totals, quantiles or other estimated statistics are retained.

Usage

fit_singlesample_preprocessor(
  X_raw,
  type = c("counts", "ct"),
  ct_limit = 40,
  ct_base = 2,
  scale = c("cpm", "none"),
  features = colnames(X_raw)
)

Arguments

X_raw

Raw specimens-by-features matrix or data frame, with unique, non-empty column names. Counts must be numeric, finite and non-negative. Ct input may include character markers, which are converted to NA.

type

Measurement type: "counts" or "ct".

ct_limit

Positive finite Ct detection limit (default 40).

ct_base

Finite exponential base greater than 1 (default 2).

scale

For counts, "cpm" divides each row by its own total over available frozen features and multiplies by one million; "none" leaves counts unchanged. Ignored for Ct conversion.

features

Ordered character vector of unique feature names present in X_raw. Defaults to all training columns.

Value

An S3 singlesample_preprocessor holding only type, features, ct_limit, ct_base, and scale.

Details

Counts of zero are non-detects. An all-zero row remains zero. Ct values that are missing, non-finite, non-numeric, or at or above ct_limit are non-detects. Their Ct is replaced by ct_limit before computing ct_base^(ct_limit - Ct), so they map to abundance 1. Negative finite Ct values below the limit are converted by the same formula.

Columns outside the frozen universe are dropped. Missing frozen columns remain absent, without imputation. For CPM, only available frozen columns contribute to that specimen's total; missing columns can therefore change its conversion. Scorer input guards determine whether support is sufficient.

Invalid inputs raise singlesample_input_error. Codes include INVALID_INPUT, EMPTY_INPUT, INVALID_FEATURE_NAMES, INVALID_PREPROCESSOR, INVALID_COUNT_VALUE (negative counts), NONFINITE_REQUIRED_VALUE (non-finite frozen count values), and NONFINITE_ABUNDANCE (conversion or count-total overflow). Errors involving measurement values report affected rows.

See also

apply_singlesample_preprocessor, deploy_singlesample

Examples

counts <- rbind(c(a = 10, b = 30), c(a = 6, b = 2))
prep <- fit_singlesample_preprocessor(counts, type = "counts")
apply_singlesample_preprocessor(prep, counts[1, ])
#> $abundance
#>           a      b
#> [1,] 250000 750000
#> 
#> $detected
#>         a    b
#> [1,] TRUE TRUE
#>
